dimension_grades.evidence: The dependency upgrade false lead is mentioned in a single sentence ('I spent some time looking through changelogs but didn't find anything suspicious') with no detail about what was investigated or why it seemed plausible.

The author never takes personal ownership of the mistake; the closest is a passive observation that 'This cache was added in a quick PR that didn't get thorough review,' which deflects blame to process rather than self.
No specific time durations are given for wrong paths; the only hint is 'took us a while to figure out' in the introduction, with no concrete hours or days mentioned.
The tone throughout is neutral and instructional ('The problem is pretty obvious when you see it') with no self-deprecating humor or wry acknowledgment of personal embarrassment.
The author lists three theories but immediately dismisses the first and jumps to heap snapshots that directly reveal the cause, with no period of genuine confusion or misreading of evidence.
The investigation goes from 'took heap snapshots' to 'noticed objects related to our caching layer' to the root cause in three consecutive sentences with no incremental clue-building.
The root cause is presented immediately in the 'Finding the Cause' section with 'The problem is pretty obvious when you see it,' landing as a premature summary rather than a payoff after tension.
No emotional states are described at any point during the investigation — no frustration, surprise, relief, or any other feeling is mentioned.
Takeaways are generic principles like 'Always monitor your memory usage' and 'Be careful with in-memory caches' rather than specific behavior changes the author now follows.
The post leads with 'Always monitor your memory usage' as its first takeaway — exactly the kind of obvious universal advice the rubric says should be omitted or acknowledged and moved past.
Takeaways like 'Heap snapshots are your friend' and 'Keep your debugging tools ready' are stated as abstract advice rather than connected to specific narrative moments.
The framing is lecturing ('Learn to use this tool before you need it,' 'The key is to not panic') rather than treating the reader as a peer who already knows the basics.
There are exactly two code snippets — the problematic code and the fixed code — each focused and earning its place in the narrative.
Neither snippet contains inline comments pointing to the critical lines; the only annotation is a comment explaining the TTL value ('// 1 hour') and cleanup interval, not the bug itself.
The problematic code (plain object cache with no eviction) and the fixed code (Map with TTL-based cleanup) are both shown, making the transformation clear.
Before the first snippet, the prose explains 'We had an in-memory cache that stored processed order results for deduplication purposes,' directing the reader to look at the caching logic.
No time of day, no environmental details, no Slack messages or UI descriptions are included; the closest is the generic '200MB of heap usage' metric.
Real tool and product names are used: Chrome DevTools, Kubernetes, Express, and Redis are all named specifically.
All key moments are summarized in retrospective narration ('The first thing I did was look at our monitoring dashboard,' 'I decided to take heap snapshots') rather than dramatized as scenes.
